requirement:
A provider failure that ends the model conversation returns
`ValidationError::Provider` with the underlying I/O error to the awaiting ask builder.
rationale:
structural: The requirement text is: "A provider failure that ends the model conversation returns `ValidationError::Provider` with the underlying I/O error to the awaiting ask builder." Every clause describes observable behavior, so I found no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence.

- **What it asks for:** which value the awaiting `ask` call yields when the provider fails. That value is the `ValidationError::Provider` variant carrying the original error.
- **Alternative implementation:** I could not find one that returns the same value and still violates a clause. Any internal design (error conversion, propagation path, delegation) that yields `Err(ValidationError::Provider(io_error))` satisfies the text. Any design that returns a different variant or drops the underlying error changes the observable result, so that is a behavioral failure, not a structural one.
- **Named type:** `ValidationError::Provider` appears in the text only as the returned value, so it is not a prescribed library, signature, or ownership structure.
- **Roots:** there are no implementation roots, and none are needed.
- **Tests:** two tests are linked to the requirement. They check that missing credentials produce `ValidationError::Provider` with the underlying message, and that a failing provider produces `ValidationError::Provider` with "permanent provider failure".
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[configured_agents_initialize_only_when_asked_and_report_setup_errors]`
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[assistant_text_and_provider_failure_cannot_become_typed_results]`

I left test adequacy to the behavioral criterion.

behavioral: The requirement has one observable obligation. When a provider failure ends the model conversation, the awaiting `ask` returns `ValidationError::Provider`, and the error carries the underlying I/O error.

- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[assistant_text_and_provider_failure_cannot_become_typed_results]` is marked `{test}`. It builds a `ToolAgent` over `Script::new(vec![None])`, whose `complete` returns `io::Error::other("permanent provider failure")`. It awaits `ctx.ask::<bool>()` and asserts the result is `Err(ValidationError::Provider(error))` with a message containing "permanent provider failure". That checks both the variant and that the underlying I/O error is preserved. A wrong variant, such as `Agent` or `Output`, or a lost or replaced error would fail it.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[configured_agents_initialize_only_when_asked_and_report_setup_errors]` is also marked `{test}`. It covers a second source of provider failure, a missing credential. It asserts that the awaited `verify` returns `ValidationError::Provider(_)` and that the message names the missing environment variable.

I found no further distinction in the text that needs its own test. Retry of transient failures such as timeouts is a different obligation. It has its own test, `a_timed_out_request_retries_and_each_success_resets_the_backoff_window`, and this requirement does not govern it.
